Hmmm So you stumbled upon Post Scriptum and want to know if it is any good.
Well Let me explain the game to you in a few words, then summarize it and give you a valuable conclusion.
To start off, this is a World War 2 Military First Person Shooter with strong emphasis on simulation and historical accuracy. 
Here in Post Scriptum. German Tiger-1 and PzKpfw V. Panthers face off against early Churchills and M4A2 Shermans, sometimes Sherman Fireflys. But not against IS-4's and M48 Patton or M26- Super-Pershings as in mediocre, arcady ww2 shooters.
You can play as an Ally (France, Brits, Americans, depending on the scenario) or as German in historical battles like the battle of Market Garden with the equipment and vehicles that were available to the specific faction by that time.
Teams(Platoons) are divided in Sections: Infantry, Logistics, Lader and Armored. You can play as an Infantry player and fulfill different roles from a front line medic able to fully heal fallen teammated to MG-Support capable of providing cover fire from a protected location. As a Logistics player, you can drive around the map and construct repair stations, ammunition boxed, fortifications as well as defensive structures and even stationary mortars. As a player of the Armored section, you will dedicate yourself and your squadmates to drive a single tank. Yes, one tank, 4 players. A gunner, A driver, A commander and one who operates the turret/Main Gun. No matter what section or role, in this game, communication is key. You are a soldier, you communicate with your squad to fulfill your tasks.
A round of gameplay takes max. 1h, but mostly between 40-50 minutes. During that time, you either try to attack and capture a set amount of bases, or you try to defend them.
As Infantry, you die from 2 shots pistol, 1 shot rifle, headshot kills you 100% regardless the weapon, everything else that hits you directly be it a tank shell, a grenade or a mortar round, kills you immediately. 
You die quick and you kill quick. Just as it would have been in real life. This is not a "you eat 9 rounds and the enemy eats 10 rounds so you win and survive" shooter. This is pretty much see first, shoot first.

Now to the technical part of the game:
You will play with up to 84 players in one lobby,
Gun Sounds are freaking awesome!
The Graphics are okay but you will struggle seeing anything beyond 600m an let's be honest, this is more than enough in most cases.
This game will make you literally shit your pants when suddenly your location is being bombarded by Ju87 Stuka Attacks or mortar strikes, Realism is a really huge topic in this game.

To Wrap it all up: 
You get an epic, yet pretty hardcore and historically accurate WW2 shooter with combined arms, teamplay, lots of communication. This game offers Great fights, good balancing and is action-packed to the fullest.

This game is something for you if:
- You like History and are interested in WW2
- You like epic realistic battles
- You value teamplay
- You own a headset/Microphone


This game is nothing for you if: 
- You prefer to play on your own
- You don't own a headset
- You value your own fun over that of others.
- You prefer Arcady shooters like CoD or Battlefield.

The mixed reviews on this I don't think are representative of the quality of this game. I'd suggest reading them and thinking critically about them before a purchase but there are some things that will go a long way to making your first time experience in PS a good one.

First, be aware of what you're buying/playing. If you want something very fast paced, and arcadey like BFV or CoD this is likely not the game for you. What PS attempts to do is build a more authentic and tactical war game experience set in WW2 and it succeeds in spades. If you like more thoughtful tactical hardcore shooters like Arma 3 and Squad, then the first time you're pinned down in a trench by mg42 fire while a stuka strafes the nearby road and grenades are going off around your ears as you're trying to understand orders from your squad leader or the platoon commander in fully spatially simulated high-def audio, you'll be hooked. The experience is really unlike any other FPS out there and that's hard to achieve considering how heavily the game is influenced by 'Squad' and it's systems. 

In the negative reviews you're going to see a smattering of specific things: "man this game is so good but it's dead" and probably "this game sucks, the movement is slow and the maps are too big and its hard to see people and get kills" and also most likely: "these devs suck theyre too inconsistent with releases and content and they haven't delivered on everything this game could be." Personally, I think the game is in a very solid place (especially for this 40% off sale) with more content in the works. The gameplay is _supposed_ to be slower, move slower etc that is by design and finally FWIW: I'm an NA player and I haven't had any trouble finding multiple filled servers any day in the last two weeks.

Let's get into what's good and what's bad:

Good
    - Audio. It. Is. The. Fucking. BEST. Totally top notch as you could expect from a game that uses most of squads engine and systems. Staggeringly excellent audio work that definitely puts most other games to shame.
    - Some of the graphics (but not all). Specifically lighting and compositing, smoke and post-processing effects are all beautiful. However, the models and textures are all fairly low poly/low-res, which i think makes sense with the massive size of the map, the team sizes, and the number of hedges, bunkers, towns, trees, bridges roads, etc that all have to exist on the gameboard at any time.
    - Gunplay. Feels pretty fantastic. The simulation here is superb top to bottom. 
    - Meta/Mechanics. Gameplay of PS is very deep. The skill-cap is quite high and there are a LOT of things you have to be aware of at any time. This game does something incredible with tactical team based combat. There are also logistics teams as well as armored division on each map and each of those jobs are immensely important to the war effort.
    - Maps. They don't really get old. They are very large, there are lots of set pieces and while they all take place during Market Garden, their sheer size and varying game modes keeps everything fresh, plus there's a nice number of them.

Cons:
    - High Skillcap. I think this is only a con if you don't like learning new things. But, it bears being mentioned. You aren't likely to join PS and end up with the highest ration on your team unless you've played lots and lots of 'Squad'.
    - Some of the graphics (but not all). As mentioned before. Some of the graphics are truly ugly.
    - Meta/Mechanics. It is quite likely that you will play PS your first time and get rolled and have a bad time unless you end up in a squad with a team that's working together. This isn't really a con of the meta and the mechanics as much as a negative point about playing games with people. There isn't really room for individuals that aren't playing their roles or following their squad leader's orders. This is not that kind of game. 
    
Hopefully this gives you an idea about the nature of the game. Don't let "this game is dead" steer you away, don't buy it if you're looking for consistent drip feeding of FPS dopamine.  And finally, Its worth way more than the $17 cost BY FAR. Support a small developer that made a really phenomenal thing here.

If you're looking for a modern milsim, play Squad
If you're looking for a WWII milsim, play Post Scriptum
If you're looking for a WWII milsim but don't want to think too much about large-scale tactics and talking on the mic, play Hell Let Loose

Each game has their place in the market. What gaming experience you're looking for will determine what game suits you, even though all these milsims seem similar.

PS is a good game so far. Nowadays, there are more players so finding a server isn't an issue anymore. I play on English speaking servers so I'm not sure about the other languages. 

A good WWII mil-sim that doesn't take too long to get into the action. I bought Hell Let Loose (HLL) and can say Post Scriptum (PS) is a more enjoyable and rewarding mil-sim. HLL has more players since it is a more casual game that requires less tactics and communication. HLL is a tad more arcadey in that sense, which brings in more players to HLL than PS because of that arcadey gameplay mentioned. I see HLL as a form of Rising Storm 2: Vietnam sometimes.

When compared to Squad, PS has more defined front lines since gamemodes are often Offensive rather than AAS or RAAS. Map design also contributes to the prominence of front lines, where bridges and rivers are more prominent and have objectives on or near them. Mobile Spawn Points in PS increase the pace of the game. In Offensive, the defending team always has a spawn point close to the objective. More importantly, FOBs seem to have an unlimited amount of supplies, which means you can build as much fortifications and emplacements as you wish without having to worry about the MGs or mortars running out of ammo and without having to do frequent logistic truck runs between the FOB and Main Base. This again also increases the pace and puts squads into the action quicker. In PS, your soldier has a canteen to regenerate stamina much quicker. This isn't in Squad either.

In the sound department, PS and Squad have an advantage over HLL. In both PS and Squad, firefights are properly loud and have good range and oomph to them. The sound design greatly adds to the realism, especially with good earphones or a decent speaker setup. The sfx in HLL are not quiet, they just don't give that same effect of power and strength, making HLL sound relatively flat. In HLL, tanks and planes sound great with lots of oomph. In PS, everything has oomph.

Overall, PS is a highly enjoyable WWII milsim which requires more tactics and communication than HLL. But because of this higher level of dedication required, PS leads itself to more rewarding experiences. The sound design in PS also achieves greater realism and power. As compared to Squad, PS puts players into the fight quicker with less worries of aspects like ammo (supplies), stamina, and spawning far away from the objective (it's less of a walking sim than Squad).

Post Scriptum is a great game for the right type of person.  It has a lot of similarities to Squad if you are familiar with that game.

The core of what this game is about is communication and teamwork.  Those two things permeate every aspect of the game, the FPS infantry gameplay, the WarThunder-esque armored gameplay, the logistics squad building structures, and the commander calling in plane, artillery, etc.  Each individual player is pretty insignificant so everyone works together to accomplish things. 

The game is more realistic than Red Orchestra or HLL, but its not a sim like ARMA.  The devs went to painstaking lengths to accurately recreate the setting.  Some of the maps are shockingly similar to their real life counterparts, the local flora is faithfully recreated, and the architecture really makes me appreciate modern building codes.  Yes the stairs really used to be that narrow.

There are 3 different types of squads, each with different gameplay.

Infantry squad.  This is the type of squad most players (27-33 per team usually) are in.  Each squad has a maximum of 9 players.  This is where the FPS action is.  Every squad has an SL, machine gun, a radio operator 2 medics, 2 fire support roles, and 2 riflemen.  Most infantry have their faction's basic rifle, which is a bolt action for everyone but the USA.  The weapons are faithfully modeled.  1 shot from a rifle is almost always lethal, an SMG will need 2-3 hits to kill.  The important thing the infantry do is they can attack and hold objectives.  Armored cars, fortifications, tanks, and artillery support can't do it without the dudes.

I have a lot of experience as an infantry SL.  Its fun, you always get to pick between a rifle and SMG(or the incredible STG44 for the germans), but I spend most of my time talking to other squad leaders, looking at my map, and getting wasted leading my guys in an assault.  I enjoy playing SL a lot, but you have a lot of things to manage, a lot more communicating to do, and you have to mark the map.  Its very different than playing as a squad member, its not just another way to get an automatic weapon.  As an SL, you actually get to make plans and can have a huge impact on the game by not only directing your squad, but getting other SLs onboard with your plan.  Its very satisfying to win the game because you came up with a winning plan that your team executed.

Armored squad.  Tanks and armored cars.  These squads have a maximum of 4 players.  Some armored vehicles only have 3 seats though.  There are a maximum of 2 armored squads per team, with a maximum of 3 armored vehicles on the field at a time.  This is my favorite part of the game.  I have experience driving, gunning, and mostly as a tank/armored car commander.  Every crew role of the vehicle except loader is filled by a player.  In a typical tank like the M4 Sherman or Tiger there is a commander, gunner, driver, and hull MG operator.  The tanks are very faithfully modeled and the new damage/penetration system coming with the tank update makes the armored game play more fun while bringing it more towards the simulator end of the spectrum.

Commander:  The commander has periscope(s) and/or a cuppola as well as the ability to turn out and use binoculars.  The commander always has the best all around view, and has no weapon to operate (except in the case of 2 man tanks like the PZ II and French tanks).  The situational awareness you have inside a tank is very poor.  You can only see the outside world through periscopes and gun sights.  The commander has the most/best optics on the tank which lets them get the best picture of whats going on so they can direct the tank.  While you may not be the one driving or shooting the gun, you are the ones that decides where the tank goes, what ammo the gunner loads, which weak spot to go for etc.

Gunner:  This is the seat everyone wants.  The gunner controls the turret and the gun.  This game uses novel controls for tank and armored cars turrets which I find really satisfying.  You aim with WASD, W elevates the gun, A slews the turret right etc.  There is a control to adjust the speed at which the turret slews and the gun elevates.  This allows you to slew the gun quickly, or very slowly for precise long range shots.  There are also different types of ammo.  AP, APC, APCBC, APCR/HVAP, HE and smoke.  I think HEAT is being added with upcoming tank patch, but am unsure.  Different vehicles have different ammo types and amounts depending on the vehicle.  In the upcoming armor update the penetration model is much more realistic, the different shell types will interact with armor differently and have different post armor effects.  Vehicles that had adjustable sights IRL have adjustable sights in the game, vehicles that had BDCs IRL have their sights accurately recreated in game.  You left click to shoot the canon and right click to shoot the coax, a feature I really like.

Driver:  This person drives the tank, and that's a big deal.  Having a good driver is important.  The upcoming armor update has done a ton to make driving fun.  Now the driver can set the throttle to whatever level they like and leave it there instead of constantly holding down W.  Each vehicle has the correct amount of gears and gearing.  Yes, the Puma has 7 forward gears, and 7 reverse gears.  Gear shifting is manual only.  Don't worry, you can't stall the motor.  The manual shifting is more engaging and gives the driver much better control.  Its especially great for handling hills and rough terrain.  There is more to driving than just taking the tank to the mark on the map.  Knowing how to angle your armor is important and can save you.  The commander's plan to escape or chase down a crippled enemy is only as good as the driver's ability to execute.

Hull MG.  IRL this person would have been operating a radio.  This is a useful seat in the tank, but the least important.  Not all tanks have a hull MG, 1 of the armored cars does.  The Hull MG primarily acts as an extra set of eyes who can defend the front of the tank against infantry threats.  You get thousands of rounds for the gun and it doesn't overheat.  The tank mount means recoil does not exist.  You may have an optic even.  The most important thing you can do is shoot anyone with an antitank weapon you see and keep your eyes peeled.  

The last type of squad is logistics.  Its limited to 5 people I think, each team only gets 1 logistics squad.  These guys move supplies around, build fobs, and do most of the building in general.  Its not flashy, but it has a big impact.  These are the guys that make all the bunkers and anti tank guns for the defense points, and make the forward repair stations that keep the armor fighting instead of driving back and forth across the map.  FOBs are critical for spawns and are strategically important.  They are also rat bastards that plant mines.

Thoughts for new players:

Don't worry about getting killed a lot and having trouble spotting people.  It takes some time.  Slow down and look before you move.  Don't be afraid to hide and sit still.  Movement is extremely eye catching and easy to spot.  

The Germans spring with their weapon in 1 hand.  The allies spring with their weapon in both hands.  This will help you figure out who to shoot.  

Check your map a lot.  I suggest rebinding it to something more ergonomic than M.  A key on your mouse or something your left hand can easily reach work well.

If you don't have a mic, get one.  Communicating with your microphone is a huge part of what makes the game engaging.

Don't play SL, get a handle on the basics of the game first.

A positiv Review ... But read carefully, this game is not for everyone. 
Post Scriptum is an ambitioned game, aiming to be one of the best realism WWII shooters out there. And it is this realism concept, that kinda makes it not suitable for every player. So if you think about getting PS, you should note the following things:
- PS is a small studio indi game and somewhat, even now oficially released, still under development
- PS is difficult to play. There is no life kill feed, enemies are often difficult to spot and your main weapon will be a rifle
- PS requires communication and teamplay. There's no such thing like rushing objectives. I highly suggest to join a clan / unit to really play the game. Do not buy the game if you are not willing to comunicate with your teammates. 
- PS is slow-paced. The rounds can easly be an hour or longer

So, why would I still suggest the game? Well, first of all I do not consider all of the things listed above as negative. The game is very comunicative, especially when using vehicles (It requires 3 players to effectively use a tank). Actually, you should be as communicative in the infantry as well, when you want to reach something. The game might still be buggy and unfinished in some points, but the developers are very ambitioned and pay attention to details. It's a simulation game, and if they keep it up, it can become one of the best things out there. I played through the entire beta/test phase, and I have actually seen progress here, so im confident that the game will further improve.

If you're looking for something similar to Call of Duty or Battlefield, this isn't for you. This is a much more realistic representation of WW2 than those games. There is no leveling, no stats that accumulate, and no K/D record. You are briefly shown your combat results at the end of a round. There is no "+100" that pops up when you kill someone. There is no aim-assist. There is an audible "pft" sort of sound if your round/bullet happens to hit an enemy. It is sort of the same sound heard in the CoD franchise. That's it. There is no radar but you do have access to a map (you will use constantly) to navigate. This is Hardcore Mode but way more hardcore.

I spent 3 hours messing around in the "Training" Mode before I ever joined a server. I suggest any new player do the same. This isn't like CoD where you learn 8 buttons and then start mowing people down. There's a lot to learn for an FPS. NO GAMEPAD, you need KEYBOARD AND MOUSE! If you try using a gamepad you're going to get SMOKED.

When you enter a round, you pick if you want to be Infantry, Armored, Logistics, etc., and then you pick a squad. There is no hero-ing, where one dude runs into the enemy spawn and yeets 6 guys. You will fight for small portions of ground for great lengths of time, alongside your squad. There are tanks, anti-tank guns/weapons, mortars, mines....pretty much everything you can think of. Communication is key and you need a mic for this game. It is possible to play without but people won't like you much. If you choose to play without a mic, make sure you at least listen to orders from squad mates. 

You will sometimes go long lengths of time without having contact with the enemy. "Camping" is part of the game, as it was in real life. Getting my first kill took forever. You work in conjunction with all the arms your squads have to try and overwhelm the enemy. It is truly team-based and extremely rewarding. Also, building fortifications is a huge part of the game. You can build rally points (re-spawn points closer to the action), MG emplacements, bunkers, trenches, and sandbags. 

Here is an example of one of my latest rounds:

I'm playing Utah Beach '44 as the Germans.....the map is huge. Several Allied landing craft come in to the south to start. Our squad quickly redeploys down to meet them. I'm just a regular infantry, equipped with a Kar98k bolt-action rifle. Really slow-firing but deadly when it hits. Our squad doesn't get far south enough to meet them head on as they land. We are at an angle, up the beach in the trenches. We all open fire on the craft as it opens. A mortar round strikes right next to it as it opens. An Allied soldier explodes into the air, blood spewing. Loud explosions and mortar fire are constant from this point on. Most of my rounds are missing, as my aim is poor, and they are pretty far from our trench. Our trench/bunker defenses are pretty far from the water. I should be waiting for them to get closer. Finally, I get a kill. One rifle round dead center mass on an Allied infantryman trying to hide behind a tank trap about 50 meters in front of me. I'm filled with elation. I got a kill!! We wind up killing off every soldier from that craft! However, another THREE are coming in to the North! Re-deploy! They wind up fighting us back and establishing a re-spawn point on the beach. We all re-group and attack the spawn point, and after a bloody battle that lasts 15 minutes, we are able to destroy the rally point and push them back into the sea!  

This game is awesome and it is easily the most realistic WW2 team-based FPS I have ever played. 

One thing to add, the community is pretty good (although too small). They are accepting of new people, just be honest and open to suggestion/direction. If someone asks for ammo, give it. If you play as an infantryman, make sure you are healing/reviving people. Don't worry about being new. Be honest about it and people will help you.

After 2000 hours, and playing this game for at least 3.5 years, I think it's time to post a short but accurate review.

I like this game. I don't love it, but it's decent. The core mechanics are okay, the map designs mediocre, community is good.

But the problem is... the developers just don't want to improve/optimise the game. Every chapter they release, it just gets worse and worse. The player base is dying because there is literally nothing new coming out in the last 6 months. The realism community + the modding community is the one keeping it alive! Not the Devs.

Even with the SDK release, it is buggy as hell. I fear that once the Armor Overhaul update comes out alongside Chapter 4, that it will break everything even more.

Game has potential. But the fact that developers do not wish to spend the time at least addressing known bugs that have been happening for at least 2 years is pretty concerning. 

This game could have overtaken HLL. But they messed up unfortunately. And we (the gamers) are partly to blame as well; because we bought their product at pre-alpha. We encouraged this practice. So it's no wonder it hasn't improved or WOW anyone.

This review has been updated as of 24.11.2019.  Last update before that time period was 03.12.2018. The thumbs down review remain negative considering the content and the patches throughout the last year - much due to the devs prioritizing new content and visual features rather than addressing the old, annoying gameplay bugs that's been reported over and over again. 

Gameplay: 

Pro's:
- Be a realistic role in a military unit, that beeing a medic, sniper, Anti-tank infantry, logistics, mine-dude, high-explosive dude, mg-man (mg = machine gunner) . 
- Multiple factions to choose from, plenty of vehicles and weapons (SS, British, Americans, Wehrmact, Polish Brigade)
- Weapons are locked and limited to roles for immersion and realism, a medic cannot use and carry a Anti-tank weapon for example. 
- huge battles, 40vs40.
- VOIP between commander, section leaders and section members to increase teamplay.
- map screen with simple markers for  commanders and section leaders to use to coordinate team and for obvious teamplay reasons. 
- Several game  modes currently and several maps with various layers (consider layers to be "missions"). 
- Have have both day and night battles aswell, increasing realism and immersion. 
- Logistics have several structures and defences which can be built to aid the team. Items such as ammo crates, repair station for armor squad or bunkers can be built, or if you want to diversify you can also block/create bottle necks with area denial objects like razorwire, barricades or tank traps. 

Both con and pro gameplay:
- The gameplay isn't nescesarry balanced in terms of values for the various objects, for example might one tank in one faction be stronger than other tanks in other factions. Some rifles shoot harder than others etc. This adds realism and immersion (WW2 wasnt balanced), but at the cost of balance. 
-  Weapons are locked and limited to roles for immersion and realism, a medic cannot use and carry a Anti-tank weapon for example.  This means players will pick roles on basis of their weapons often, and not because they actually want to play "that" role.  (Ps. People tend to pick sniper but just dont play with the rest of their section at all, as an example). This needs to be adressed some way, but I will get back to it later. 



Con's gameplay: 
- Vehicles have unrealistic physics. Want to drive 60 km/h trough nasty mud ? no problem. The only thing that affects vehicle speed is if it's uphill/down hill terrain and their base speed/accceleration. Terrain have no impact.
- you can flip (reset their position a bit left/right) vehicles over tank traps. Reported and no action done to fix this. Reported in 2018.  Edit: Reported in 2019. No action still. 
- Placing static machinegun emplacement in buildings (on some open maps buildings are the best and only viable cover for infantry) is not possible in 9/10 windows because the window frames are too high. This have been reported and isn't prioritized by the devs to fix. Edit: It's also a realistic thing static machineguns can do - in ww2 these machineguns could change their elevation. In Post Scriptum they cannot. 
- There is ways to dupe things as logistic such that you can get infinite vehicles/constructions as attackers for example  through FOBS(allthough time consuming process). This is a gamebreaking bug if exploited.
- Various fortifications gets destroyed way too easely (razorwire gets destroyed by grenades fore 
=============================
Let's talk about teamplay. To me this is the most important part in the game, if there is no teamplay, the game is essentially like CoD or Battlefield, just random chicken players running around blasting each other. So, does the game have the tools and features in it's backbone to actually make sure the game have teamplay ?   

i will split this into teamplay and community management: 

Community management: 

Lets quickly recap what some other heavely teambased games do to make sure people can cooperate, and how those deals with potential evildoers and trollers : 
- Reporting badly behaving players  (Dota 2, Rocket League)
- Kicking from server through votes /admin kick ( Mount and blade, Arma3 etc.) 
- In a hierarchical game, one does not want people to get into roles that have great power or influence over other players experience of the game without having a way to counter them. In this case, I'm refering to section leaders ( Squad leaders) and the platoon commander (with his artillery).

POST SCRIPTUM does not have any ways to manage badly behaving players, except with admin kick (and the servers are community hosted for the record). There is no way to deal with bad players if there is no admin online. 

Allright, but what about the teamplay? 
Where shall I begin? 
- Static map markers which last as long as someone wants is impossible, since every marker dissapears after 2-3 minutes. This makes using the map harder. 
- There's no way to mute other channels in VOIP, making playing section leader (listeining to commander channel + your soldiers in the section ) a listening excersice. 
- The platoon commander doesnt have any ways to give orders to his section(s) whatsoever, except talking to them. No assignment to map markers, no way to block a spawn point if you want to force players to go somewhere else or demote a badly behaving section leader. In general, no way to actually give orders and to make sure they're followed). 
- Some things in the game are not addressed at all which requires teamplay. The game currently utilizes "MSP's" as a spawn feature,and these spawn at the main base and need to be brought to the objective. However, in many games noone takes these things and drive them to the objective. The reason ?  1) people are not aware they're at the base 2) Nobody wants to do it as long as there is a spawn point available at objective. And then you can spawm in commander channel and ask someone to take it, but noone does, not even when called out by name. Eventually, you will experience teams loosing many objectives because people are not able to enforce orders on other, lower-ranked people. 

I've suggested to the devs many times to solve these issues, but they are not prioritized or ignored (basically the same thing).  Basically what i'm trying to say : 
POST SCRIPTUM dev team does NOT prioritize features which enchance and makes teamplay easier despite claiming to be a game about teamplay and cooperation. It does not even come close to how other games (even the ones less mil-sim based) approach teamplay issues - dota 2 makes sure reporting is a feature to dodge assholes, arma 3 have drawing and map markers, and Savage XR have commander votes and impeachment of badly behaving players in position of power.  

TLDR: 
The tools in the game to ensure teamplay is present is very poor, and does not live up to the expectation I had when I bought the game. The gameplay and immerion is great, but the teamwork essentialls are lacking greatly aside from the VOIP feature and a map menu with poor selection of options to coordinate a team with. There is also some animation and minor gameplay glitches (EAC authentication issues on connection to server), falling through the map and getting camera glitches as infantry issues. THe game feels very raw and unpolished. 

The current state can be said like this: 
 If you like CoD or Battlefield, you might want to consider this game (but expect some walking/running). If you like teamplay like me, you will be dissapointed. The game tries to be different than CoD and BF, and does this well in terms of a lot of the features, but lacks the teamwork features to make all these minor gameplay features work together for the team.
Edit as of 24.11.2019 : the engine upgrade to 4.21 have increased performance across the board, which was needed. However, the devs still dont adress serious gameplay issues in the core game, and that alone is reason for a negative review.

A World War 2 game in the style of SQUAD; Not entirely mil-sim but not entirely arcade, it bridges the gameplay gap between battlefield and arma quite well. Providing a deeper level of team-level stategic and squad-level tactical gameplay than a game like BATTLEFIELD provides, without falling into the more mil-sim niche like that a game such as ARMA sits in. 
I enjoy it. 

-- It is hosted on dedicated servers and utilises a server browser. It has no leveling up, or matchmaking of any kind.
-- Matches typically last between 30 minutes and 90 minutes.
-- Team sizes of 40 v 40 (possibly more in future).
-- Optimization is rough, but improving. 
-- Multi-Crew Tank Combat (though limited to two 4-man squads per team). Implemented very well, giving (at maximum) a tank a driver, main gunner, hull gunner, and tank commander.  Tanking is exciting, with visibility being low and restricted to viewports when buttoned up. 
-- Only a few maps, however each map is very large contains a dozen+ variations changing sides and capture paths, allowing them to be very versitile and keeping them feeling fresh. 
-- Microphones are pretty much mandantory to play the game, due to the constant need to communicate with your squadmates and the suddenness and quickness of firefights disallowing typed-out updates in any reasonable manner.
-- Most people i've met are welcoming to newcomers and forgive mistakes.

-- Its not a game for everyone. There are periods of 5+ minutes where you wont see an enemy at all. Theres a lot of walking. Theres a lot of waiting. Theres a lot of hiding behind a bush because you dont want to be seen. There are times you'll walk for 5 minutes and get popped in the skull from out of nowhere by someone who found a good place to post up on defense (sometimes you'll be the guy waiting 5 minutes to do the popping). Sometimes theres an incredible front-line war. With bullets whizzing and adrenaline pumping on both sides, running through streets lined with machine guns and past explosions to secure a point. But they're both things you're going to experience, and you have to be okay with them both. Because its all part of the fun of the game.

-- Team-play is incredibly important, working with your squad is incredibly important, and objective-based gameplay trumps all others. The game is about listening to your teammates and working with them to get a goal done. Its all collaberative. 

--There are no level up rewards, there is no carrot for you to chase. The game is entrely held within each match. It is a game you play because you want to play it, not because you want a new skin, or a new badge. And if you're okay with that, if that type of slower-paced (but not slow) gameplay is something you enjoy, its incredibly fun. Esspecially if you find have a good squad to play with. 

I've had a lot of fun with it, and have 98ish hours in the beta client from pre-release to add to the number at the top of my review. I'll continue to put more into it. Its not the most polished game, its not the most optimised game, its for a niche crowd. 
But I think its its fun.
Oh boy do i think its fun.

I read a lot of discussions on Reddit and Youtube about HLL vs PS before buying this game. I came across a lot of fanboys of both games which did not help me at all to get an objective view.
I am just a guy who wants a good experience of WW2 theme. I only care about the product. So here is my  take on both games.

* Graphics:
I think Squad 44 is not worth 30 USD. I consider it as an investment hoping OWI will develop it further.
Graphics are not good. Some bushes are cube shaders with grass texture on them, looks like I made the game in Unreal Engine. Buildings are empty with no interior objects like desks/lamps/other props.

My opinion: I don't really have a problem with empty buildings or inferior graphics but this kills immersion. One of the hot topics about HLL vs PS was immersion and people claimed PS has better immersion. Sorry but HLL wins this for me. HLL has much better scenery / graphics and cinematic moments.

I want to point out, in PS you can actually use buildings/windows to shoot from, unlike most buildings in HLL. And there are some invisible colliders between passages in HLL, so even if you see nothing blocking you, you cannot actually pass to other side which is frustrating.

* Communication:
One of the claims was PS had better communication than HLL and people said no one talks in HLL / everyone talks in PS. Well no, both wrong. HLL has a lot of comm between Squad leaders and Commander, I agree rest of the squad may remain silent but they follow orders. I had half of my games in PS which only 3/9 people talking in squad. It really depends on the people you get on the server. It is just a coin flip. And don't forget that more players play HLL and PS has more of a fanbase. When you have a larger community you get more casuals. One might argue this is a bad thing, I would argue I can just join any server and start playing immediately. If any point Squad 44 will have the same player count, same problem will arise.

My opinion: No need trying to bash HLL on this. PS is slightly better with comms, don't expect a spectacular amount of teamwork here too. As I said: more players, more casuals.

* Player Count: Go to steam charts and you can check it yourself. As of now, HLL has much bigger community.

* Combat:
So one of the hot topics was that HLL was said to be too arcadey. They said HLL has no stamina bar so you just run and gun. Let me tell you, having to drink from your canteen between changing positions or before engaging does not make it less arcadey, it is just a feature which I have no problem with, it reminds me to stay hydrated irl.
I can ADS zoom in PS while moving, however HLL does not let you ADS zoom when you move. But no one talks about this. One realistic improvement PS has is, when your stamina is low, you cant ADS at all or aim accurately when you ADS.

I don't really care about sound design (PS is better), animations (HLL is better) or anything else. My top priorities are the ones above.

To summarize:
Graphics and Immersion = HLL is better
Player Count = HLL is much better
Communication = PS is slightly better
Combat = Consider it as equally fun.

I may update my review as I play Squad 44 more, and I will keep playing both games.

Conclusion:
Try Hell Let Loose first if you are interested in WW2 theme. If you enjoy it, I recommend you to try this game out too.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Gameplay[/h2]

Since I am someone who is looking at a game's [b]gameplay[/b] first whilst considering its quality, I am naturally going to tackle this subject first.

While Squad 44 is a First Person Shooter game, it emphasizes heavily on the communication, coordination, combat awareness that a Military Game can provide.

In other words, no, you are not going to win because you have the most kills, but rather because you made sense of the chaos around you, you and your team, and took advantage of every opportunities that shown themselves during the battle.

This alone is really satisfying.

[i]"But wait? Why don't you play Hell Let Loose then? Isn't it the same?"[/i]

Well no, definitely not, I am even arguing in favor of Squad 44 on the gameplay part (and as well in other aspects but we'll get back to it).

[b]Why? Why am I asking this rhetorical question in the first place?[/b]

Hell Let Loose is indubitably Squad 44's direct active competitor when it comes to WW2 Milsims, hence the comparison here.

[b]Hell Let Loose is a game I would qualify as very linear:[/b]

Each objective are devided in sectors, that implies a clear frontline, is this a good thing?
Well it's boring, simply put; Opportunities for flanking are really restricted and predictable from the enemy.

Hell Let Loose has too much of a Meta, hold this area, if you do not, you are bound to lose, and this is annoying.

There are a lot of other points to be made here, as in gameplay superiority Squad 44 offers over Hell Let Loose, but this is a review of Squad 44, so let's not get ourselves lost.

[i]If you want to know more about my views on Squad 44 vs Hell Let Loose, let me know in the comments.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The art[/h2]
[i]I include in this section sound design, visuals, music, etc...[/i]

Squad 44 is a blessing to the ears, I mean it.

No other games made me feel stimulated and immersed in the current action of the battlefield as this game, it is top notch.

The  MG42 sound especially takes me to another epoque, I can not stress this enough.
Not to mention the tank shell ricocheting.

As far as the visual goes, the game is gorgeous, the maps are beautiful and feel alive.

On the topics of maps, they are really good; They offer a lot of point of interests, difference in elevations to play with, and landmarks that can be taken advantage of.

Yes some of the building may feel empty, I never considered this as a problem however.

The game features appealing music, but it is not its main focus however.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Community[/h2]

So this is when the review tackles a bit of a problematic aspect, the main one I believe, the one that is cited by the negative reviews the most in my opinion.

The Community is not bad per se, or toxic rather, but it is lacking in quantity:

[b] There are times of the day in which the game is simply unplayable[/b]
Due to a lack of player base, the game suffers from a chronic low state, in which no servers have enough players to play a full game, and is stuck in a "seeding" mode.

This to me is the main problem of Squad 44.

But really then, does that make it a bad game?
I think it is a far stretch to think so.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Hope[/h2]

This is section is a love letter to Squad 44, and a plea to the community, and interested buyers, to support the game by any means, or just by playing it even.

Squad 44 deserve more love than it is currently getting, not by the developers, but by the community.

I am optimistic that with good communication with the developers and the community, we can build a strong player base back up, and live a new era of Squad 44.

Yes you can play Squad 44, and you should if you are even remotely interested in milsims, but in full honesty you won't be able to play whenever you want, that's the only issue that persists to me.

I love Squad 44. It is genuinely one of my favorite WWII games I have ever played, which makes leaving a negative review frustrating.

A lot of us fell in love with this game back when it was Post Scriptum around 2018. It has always had a smaller player base, but the foundation was there. The immersion, the tank combat, the sound design, the scale, the weapons, the vehicles, and the overall atmosphere are still some of the best you will find in a WWII shooter.

The problem is not the game itself. The problem is the oversight and direction.

Since Offworld Industries picked it up and rebranded it as Squad 44, there have been good ideas, but the execution has been rough. The Pacific maps were huge and a great addition in theory. There is an unbelievable amount of weapons and vehicles across each nation. The tank combat is still top notch, and when the game is firing on all cylinders, you will not find many WWII games that feel this immersive.

But the biggest issue has never really been solved: no officially hosted servers.

For a game with such a small player base, forcing the community to carry the entire server structure is absurd. Most of the time you are stuck playing on one or two community servers, and even those are not always fully populated. Offworld should have been able to capitalize on this game and grow it beyond a few hundred dedicated players, especially with the resources behind them now.

That is what makes this so disappointing. Squad 44 is a gem. It has the bones of something incredible. But it desperately needs better direction, better oversight, and a team that actually understands what the player base wants.

I still love this game, but I cannot recommend it in its current state.

This game used to be the pinnacle of tactical WWII shooters. Back when it was Post Scriptum, I had a smooth experience with constant 120–180 FPS. Even under heavy artillery fire, explosions, and intense combat, it never dropped below 90 FPS. It felt crisp, responsive, and professional.

Now, under current development, it has become a technical disaster:

Performance Decay: Currently, I’m only getting 90 FPS while idling on the shooting range—and even that is riddled with constant micro-stutters.

Multiplayer Mess: As soon as I join a 100-player server, the game collapses. I am stuck at 30 FPS. In a hardcore shooter where every millisecond counts, 30 FPS with input lag is a death sentence.

Broken Priorities: Instead of fixing the foundation, the devs keep pushing new content like maps and factions. What is the point of a new map if it runs like a slideshow?

The Declaration of Failure: If the developers actually prioritized optimization and core engine fixes over fluff, this game would have 5 to 10 times the current player count. People want to play this, but they can't because it’s fundamentally broken.

Final Warning: Stop adding content to a sinking ship. Fix the performance or this game will continue its death spiral until it’s eventually removed from the market. I cannot recommend buying this "slideshow" until the devs prove they care about playability more than just adding more maps.

If you want to save the player base, here are the technical areas that need immediate attention over any new content:

PSO Caching (Stutter Mitigation): Implement robust Pipeline State Object caching to prevent shader compilation stutters during gameplay. Shaders should be pre-compiled to ensure a smooth combat experience.

Draw Call Bottlenecking & HLODs: The current number of Draw Calls is choking the CPU. You need to optimize HLODs (Hierarchical Level of Detail) and batch meshes more efficiently, especially on dense maps, to reduce the overhead.

Game Thread Optimization: The game is heavily bottlenecked by the Game Thread (Single-core dependency). Calculations for animations, physics, and complex blueprints need to be offloaded to Worker Threads to utilize modern multi-core CPUs.

Network Relevance & Replication: Optimize Net Relevance Distance. The client shouldn't be processing data for actors or players that are miles away. This would significantly reduce the CPU load in 100-player environments.

Audio Engine Overhead: Streamline the audio channel management. During heavy artillery barrages, the UE4 audio system currently consumes too many resources. Implementing better sound culling is essential.

Conclusion: I don't want to leave a negative review because I love the core of this game, but it needs to be playable. Please prioritize engine optimization over new content. Fix the foundation so we can enjoy the house.

Review:
First off, congrats to the devs for accomplishing the full release. It is no easy task to create a video game, even one that utilizes the mechanics and engine of another game. I wish them the best of luck.

With that said, here were my expectations for the lens of the review:
- A WWII game with Squad & Project Reality level of teamwork and communication. 
- An Attack/Defend mode that places emphasis on a true Attack/Defense experience 
- The promotion and usage of the Deployables feature to create different gameplay experiences and tactical decisions for both teams

Why I do not recommend this game:

Post Scriptum has alot of potential and it pains me to write this review, but I cannot in good conscience keep silent. While I try to follow my feelings of love and respect of the game I have followed, hyped and purchased for the past two years, I cannot ignore the facts and feed cognitive dissonance.  

The issues that hold back Post Scriptum from creating my expectations:

Teamwork:  PS lacks it. On average only about 1 out of every 4 games I have played have cohesive Squad leads, logistics and armor. The other 3 out of 4 instances I experienced a lack of communication or almost no attempts at coordination between either the leadership (PC to SL, SL to SL) or unit (SL to Squad members & vice versa).

While this problem may reduce over time, the problem is not  the communities fault completely. It's rather a symptom exasperated by Post Scriptum's game mechanics.  These are a combination of the Spawn and Logistical systems, Defensive structure HP pools and terrain features.

1) Spawn mechanics: While I can see why devs went with the Mobile Spawn Point (MSP) in theory, it does not work in practice.  Instead of creating an authentic front line from various areas from game to game it promotes disorganized gameplay, lone wolfing, and the ability for both attackers and defenders to appear from all directions very quickly.  The result is no observable or general idea of a "Front Line" which is vital for a game that revolves around an attack/defend experience.  

The main game mode is Operations, which is an attack/defend game mode similiar to Squad's Invasion mode (or dare I even say Battlefield series assault modes).  The problem here is that there is very little difference between attacking and defending.  Why? First let's look at a very general overview:  
- Attackers have access to 2 Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) to respawn (which can be built anywhere on the large map) and multiple MSPs
- Defenders have no access to FOBs. Instead they have 1-2 MSPs and a randomized temporary Spawn point approximately 600 meters away from the objective (it is usually near the next capture point)
- Attackers cannot "capture" the next point for a few minutes, but can enter the area
- There is no planning mode where Defenders have a chance to discuss tactics or build defenses.  As soon as the round starts, weapons are free.

As a result, most of the games I have played look similiar to this scenario:

Attacker Logistics Squad drives straight into enemy territory toward future capture points, usually unharrased due to the map size.  They place future FOBs as Ninja spawn areas.  At the same time after the Attacking Infantry/armor Squads capture a point(albiet in a chaotic, unplanned fashion), the team simply has 1 player hop in their MSPs and rush to the back or flanks of the next cap point.  This gives the defenders very little time to reorganize and stage their next defense.  It also creates a situation where attackers will be advancing from at least three directions within 1-4 minutes. This issue limits the player count engaging one another (for an epic confrontation moment) and results to many small skirmishes.  The problem is that the game should create the former most times, but rather creates the latter. You'll find yourself in constant instances of lone wolf infiltrators shooting you in the back, casually sprinting into the house you thought was secure or only engaging 1-5 enemies at a time.  

To make the situation worse, the defenders lack of a FOB forces their team to do the SAME thing attackers are doing: rushing their MSP to the back or sides of the cap point to sprint in and capture it.  

Instead of the game mechanics to allow Defensive FOBs which would be placed on or near the point (thereby having structures built around them)  we get gameplay experiences where both Attackers and Defenders quickly sprint in from everywhere while a few lone wolf ATs or half of a squad run around the edges of a cap point to hunt MSPs (It's an area where almost all MSPs are placed and undefended)

As Attackers have multiple MSPs and FOBs, they win most maps. (I've seen posts in the forums that counter that with European server players claiming games are usually close and defenders generally win. I play on NA servers so I cannot speak to that, I would like to know how that situation happens...)

2) Logistics: Defensive structure building is limited to the Logistics Squad.  This mechanic limits the player count of placing actual defensive structures in or around points to attempt and defend it.  In contrast, PS's sibling, Squad, does not feature a dedicated Logistics squad (yet). This allows the Squad leaders to dedicate who will be building defensive structures at a given moment, take turns or work together to place defensive structures in an area at the same time. Thus allowing a quick build of structures to create areas of inaccessibility, kill zones, etc. around a capture point.
 
3) Defenses: As for defenses, they are destroyed too quickly and need a small health pool increase. A few mortar rounds or even one airstrike will immediately negate them.  This leads one to question why they should invest time building them in the first place (which may be part of the reason why they are barely utilized)

4) Terrain Features:  The maps are big and detailed (apparently even close to the terrain features of 1944) but do not create natural choke points or restrict movement to encourage tactical hypothesis of where a tank may drive through or where a squad may attempt to enter/flank. The result leads to little way for organic tactical points of interest or large, intense firefights.

While all of these issues may not cause the big problem with gameplay in PS , in combination they most definitely hinder any chance at achieving gameplay expectations. Do you like singing Katy Perry, Miley Cyrus and The Backstreet Boys in your car?! Well good, because every Logistics run or half-track trip to the front lines is an equally new and special experience with the player base of Post Scriptum. The game is filled with hardcore military sim players, but they are equally as down to have some fun at the beginning of the round or in between fire fights.
This game feels genuine to real world combat, with a bunch of grunts and jar heads running around trying to make light of a bad situation. 
The combat is sporadic, but ferocious and will get you dodging MG fire in your computer chair. As you take well place shots at the enemy combatants 200 yards out, your heart rate will elevate due to the depth and volume of the sounds. They are next level for a first person shooter and are second only to the real thing. 
Now lets say you survived your first engagement, you may find yourself huddled in a trench with your battle buddy laughing about your best friend, who's legs just got cleaved clean off by the blast of an enemy grenade. As you move to regroup you will find yourself staring at the awesome power of a well place artillery barrage. The effects and graphics in this game will have you hoping the friendly Firefly to your left side will catch a round from the Flak 88 and erupt into a ball of flames, as the ammunition heats up from the awesome blaze the ammunition will start to cook off and send tracers into the night sky, like roman candles on the 4th of July. 
Some games will suck, as your team will be poorly organized and command is nowhere to be found. Other games will be satisfying victories as you, your new found friends, and your squad lead efficiently coordinate assault after assault until the back bone of the opposing force snaps. 

But seriously, this game is the most genuine World War II FPS to date, the effects, sounds, and gun play will have you asking for more. This game is based heavily on team work on REQUIRES a microphone. You will have to experience more than one round to get an understanding of this game, don't give up after one failed round. Learn from your experience and mistakes and take that into the next round of combat.

I come to Post Scriptum from many long PR and Squad.
Post Scriptum takes everything these two games have built and honed and keeps pushing the ball forward.
Its a masterpiece.
Heres what makes it great:

History is the theme and its respected. Nothing out of place or time. 

The skill curve is severe. If you want the opportunity to get better and distinguish your performance this is the game. The damage model is very unforgiving, almost everthing is iron sights, many manual bolt actions, the scope sway and suppresion and stamina mechanics make it hard to do well.

There are many different roles and different ways to contribute. You can play as a frontline rifleman and be a grunt. You can shoulder the responsibility of leading a squad. You can be a sapper and try to destroy enemy assets with explosives. Drive truck and build machinegun nests as a logistics guy. Mortars. Team leader. Sniper. Tanker, etc etc etc.

The teamplay is naturally enforced by game mechanics. The decision to do well/ try to win will naturally draw you into symbiotic and cohesive squad and team interaction.

Theres many layers of play. You have your personal performance as a contribution to the squad. The squad delivers results as a unit and contributes to the team. The teams square off in a battle where the side that can deliver the best coordinated effort will probably win. Tug of war is less of a teamplay game than PS.

The maps are beautiful and well thought out. Theres lots of room for creative solutions to difficult problems. From dense cityscapes to farmland to wooded areas theres great variety. The devs have also built it carefully to facilitate the play like a well planned paintball course. You feel liike this is how western europe looks.

When you play the game you will feel the passion the devs have for the project. I've talked to many people I've played 1500 hours of squad with and they agree Post Scriptum has more "Soul". I think the devs made the game they wanted to play.

The bads:
It's not done, but theyre still building it.
It's not optimized but theyre still building it.
If you want fast arcade action or simple casual play you might not like it. But you might!

Don't hesitate youve spent more on bad pizza.

Post Scriptum was so much fun when I started playing it. The game worked great, handling of vehicles was alright, the community made it fun, and to be engaged in a game where communication and teamwork go a long way was so new and amazing to me, no other game matched it. I played it so much and convinced my friends to get it too, and we teamed up and played a good portion of it as tank crew, but other times as a medic or squad leader.

But, after a while, nothing happened. No new updates, silence, stagnation. A community, that went apart and got into other similar games. I was excited about the new engine update, cause of the potential, I was excited, for the armored update, cause of the potential. But it all was for nothing, and in turn, made the game worse. Handling of the vehicles feels off, a Stug IV barely moves, if you are a little bit right or left, losing all its momentum in an instant. I sincerely cannot believe, how you can turn something from ''functional but bad'' to ''barely functional'' from vehicles handling ''bad'' to ''worse'' after a huge dedicated update for it.

The infantry gameplay can be fun but it's nothing special, the vehicle gameplay can be, but now you have to actively fight your tank as a driver. Vehicles feel worse after the ''big'' armored update. The Torque and grip to the ground feel off, Tanks get stuck where they definitely shouldn't. The player base is dwindling at this time of writing the review, and this game feels like a worse version of it than the past. I wanted this game to capture its potential, cause there is a great recipe for an engaging, fun, and realistic take, but all these opportunities were thrown out. It disappoints me greatly, cause I wanted this to succeed. I was a dedicated player, now give up on the game, and I have way more fun playing its competitors.

If you are thinking about getting it, I suggest looking at other games in this category strongly. Whether or not it's Modern or WW2 as well, I strongly suggest staying away from Post Scriptum, the other games will be worth your time, and money. Remember to always make an informed purchase on the product you buy.

I was someone, who got his friends to play, someone who took the roles nobody wanted to take responsibility for, I enjoyed my time, I loved it, and I wanted it to grasp its potential, but after the stagnation, I only became more bitter and bitter. This now is a personal farewell to the game. Thanks to the Devs for trying, and thanks to the community for making it a great experience.

Alright. Real simple for everyone who's looking into buying this game. I will only present facts and remember that these facts are subject to change as the devs continue to patch this game frequently.

PROS:
- FAIR PRICE. For a game that doesn't have a singleplayer you can't argue a $30 price tag.
- No other WW2 game on the steam market like this
- The shooter aspect of this game is extremely fun (however it is realistic so if 2 hit kills isn't your thing then look away)
- The vehicle combat aspect of this game is absolutely amazing. You will have to work with your squad to properly operate every aspect of the vehicle. A well oiled machine is a killing machine.
- The logistics gameplay is very fun and relaxing but definitely only for the advanced players. If you mess this up you will most likely mess up your entire teams chances at winning.
- Beautiful graphics
- Beautiful array of vehicles and weapons
- Frequent patching and updates
- Devs that are listening to the community
- Great immersion for WW2 fanatics/buffs

CONS:
- The game is fully released but feels like it's still in beta.
- Weapon, vehicle, and player models aren't very balanced yet. Expect the Brits to have the advantage.
- The driving mechanic for this engine (same as squad) is really not that great and pretty frustrating but is getting better with time and patches.
- Overall mechanics of gameplay definitely need work as a few individuals currently have the ability to mess the entire team up if they please with no punishment.
- Game is not very optimized and will be very taxing on mid to low tier gaming rigs.
- Some maps are still very glitchy however devs are actively creating patches to address these issues, so more like a half con.

Overall I would definitely recommend this game for the price it's currently at $30 I believe. I have a lot of fun with it and a lot of frustrations, but as the devs continue to patch the game and release new assets, it keeps me coming back and having a lot of fun.
